chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: What a mellophone looked like, and hocking the banjo
summary: He describes the mellophone and baritone horn, and says he hocked his gold-plated Paramount banjo.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Tell us real quick what a mellophone
looked like in those days--- Well, it looked like a French horn, you know--
It looked like a French horn--
Yeah but it went under your arm-- but now they make them upright--- and they make them with bells that are adjustable and everything now.
Are they close to what's now a baritone horn?
No - no - they were like a trombone really - about the same kind of a sound and then, of course, now they make them with the smaller bells, which gives it a more of a trombone sound---
What is that thing that Eddie Hubble plays---
That's a baritone. Is it like that---
Yeah - no it's not like that--- it's an alto horn.

Anyway, he'd build some arrangements around me and he sort of made me kind of a feature and I was very thrilled about that, of course. And, at this point, the banjo is long gone-- I just gave us that thing -- as a matter of fact, I hocked it --
And, that was the end of that and I'm sorry I did because it was a Paramount - a gold plated Paramount and a very hard instrument to find these days - you know.
